title: redwood-poc-weekly-sync-benchmark-review-vs-baseline-provider
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing benchmark results vs baseline provider. Redwood SE walked through latency and throughput numbers, discussed tuning (batching, KV caching, quantization), and next steps: run on-prem comparison, share updated spreadsheet and security docs, and schedule a deeper perf run with larger seq lengths.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated benchmark spreadsheet with per-model breakdown (Maya) by 2026-03-04
Redwood SE to schedule on-prem test window with Astra infra team (Diego) tentative week of 3/16
Astra to confirm dataset and seq length distribution for on-prem run (Liam) by 2026-03-06
Redwood to share SOC2 + KMS encryption docs and network diagram (Maya) by 2026-03-05
action_items: Maya Chen: share updated benchmark spreadsheet and security pack - due 2026-03-04
Diego Ramos: prepare on-prem run checklist and perf script - due 2026-03-12
Liam O'Connor: provide sample workload distribution and headers for seq length - due 2026-03-06
Priya Patel: coordinate infra access & firewall exceptions for test window - due 2026-03-10
transcript:
00:00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we know you're busy so we'll kick off, quick roll call?
00:00:05 Liam O'Connor: yep Liam here, sorry bit of background noise, head of ML at Astra Health.
00:00:08 Priya Patel: Priya, platform eng.
00:00:11 Evan Brooks: Evan here, CTO.
00:00:13 Diego Ramos: Diego from Redwood SE, hi all.
00:00:16 Maya Chen: cool thanks, agenda: go over last week's benchmark numbers, latency/throughput vs your baseline provider, then tuning notes and decide next steps.
00:00:30 Diego Ramos: quick note, we re-ran the 1k qps baseline with the new batching settings and KV caching enabled for the prefix-heavy prompts you gave us. I'll share slides after.
00:00:45 Liam O'Connor: nice, curious about p99 numbers, baseline provider p99 is roughly 420 ms for the 512 token average, right?
00:00:55 Priya Patel: yes that's what we've been seeing from BaselineCloud during peak.
00:01:00 Diego Ramos: okay so our numbers: median latency for Redwood-hosted model variant rwd-7b-q4 was ~120ms for 128 tokens, median at 512 tokens bumped to 260ms, and p99 at 512 tokens was 370ms in that same config. Note transcription: some labels in the export say rwd-7b-q4-mlk which is a small naming mismatch in the automation.
00:01:30 Evan Brooks: so p99 is better than baseline but not by a ton, curious on throughput.
00:01:34 Diego Ramos: (laugh) thanks, typo, 00:01:34 — throughput at 1k concurrent requests we saw sustained 920 rps with steady-state batching; with burst policy enabled hit 1.1k briefly. Baseline provider plateaued at 700 rps in our tests for the same model.
00:01:55 Liam O'Connor: are those exact same instance types/network egress? our baseline was on BaselineCloud n2-highmem-ish instances not GPUs, so wanted to confirm apples-to-apples.
00:02:10 Maya Chen: good call — not identical. Our hosted runs used A100-backed ded instances; baseline numbers came from the spreadsheet BaselineCloud sent which were GPU-backed but different infra. We'll add a per-instance comparison column in the spreadsheet.
00:02:30 Priya Patel: show us the effect of KV cache — that's our main interest because we have lots of conversational prefix reuse.
00:02:38 Diego Ramos: sure. With KV/prefix caching enabled we saw token emission latency drop about 15-25% on average for prompts with 80% prefix reuse; in live runs p50 goes down ~30ms and p99 improves ~50-60ms depending on sequence length. However cold-starts still penalize — the first request that populates cache is similar to baseline.
00:03:10 Liam O'Connor: that's promising. What about quantization — you mentioned q4/q8 tradeoffs earlier?
00:03:20 Diego Ramos: right. The q4 runs (int4-like) improved throughput per-GPU by ~1.6x and latency improved ~20% at 512 tokens. But quality slightly degraded on our rouge-like eval — a 2-3% generation quality dip on the clinical summarization prompts. We recommend q4 for non-critical pipelines and q8 for production accuracy-sensitive flows.
00:03:48 Evan Brooks: any observed hallucination increases with q4?
00:03:51 Diego Ramos: small uptick, yes, most pronounced on open-ended prompts. For structured extraction you were fine. We'll annotate which eval prompts had divergence.
00:04:05 Maya Chen: quick interjection — security/perf tradeoffs: we can run private (VPC) deployment to match your network egress and also do on-prem for fully comparable results. That's on the table if you'd like to proceed.
00:04:18 Priya Patel: we'd prefer on-prem for the pilot if possible so we can run against our exact infra and observe network latencies.
00:04:25 Liam O'Connor: agree — also need SOC 2 and KMS docs before infra access.
00:04:30 Maya Chen: yes we'll send security docs today.
00:04:35 Diego Ramos: back to benchmarks — I want to point out the seq length distribution matters a lot. Your workload has bimodal distribution: 60% at ~128 tokens (short questions) and 40% at ~512 tokens (summaries). We ran separate mixes and combined mixes; combined mix p99 looks worse because the large sequences dominate compute.
00:05:05 Priya Patel: that's our mistake maybe we previously sent a single avg. We'll share the real distribution CSV.
00:05:10 Liam O'Connor: question on batching: what's Redwood's approach to latency-sensitive small requests? we can't tolerate 200ms added queuing.
00:05:18 Diego Ramos: we use adaptive batching — if latency SLO indicates small latency windows we'll lower batch sizes and prioritize latency; throughput mode increases batch windows. In your tests we used a conservative latency policy which is why throughput wasn't fully maxed out; we can flip to throughput to show the different tradeoff curves.
00:05:38 Evan Brooks: can you show a graph of latency vs throughput points?
00:05:40 Diego Ramos: yes, slide 4 in the deck has a qps vs p99 curve per model; I'll include the CSV. For example at 500 rps the p99 on rwd-7b-q4 is 240ms, at 1k rps it's 370ms.
00:06:02 Liam O'Connor: what about cost — rough unit cost comparison? baseline provider claims cheaper per-1M tokens.
00:06:10 Maya Chen: short answer: unit economics vary with cache hit rate and batching. With 70% KV hit rate and good batching we estimate 30-45% lower per-token cost vs baseline in our runs; I'll add per-token cost columns with assumptions to the spreadsheet.
00:06:27 Priya Patel: include assumptions: GPU hourly cost, batch size, cache hit rate, egress.
00:06:34 Diego Ramos: will do. Also note dedicated/dedicated-reserve pricing would further lower per-token costs if you commit.
00:06:45 Evan Brooks: ideal next step: do the on-prem test to remove infra variance and push longer seq lengths 1024 tokens to see scaling.
00:06:55 Maya Chen: agreed. Diego, can you outline the on-prem test plan?
00:06:58 Diego Ramos: sure. We'll need: (1) access window and firewall exceptions, (2) a VM/container image and perf harness we'll run, (3) the dataset and seq length distribution, (4) target qps points to test, and (5) metrics collection — we prefer your Prometheus or we'll ship logs. We'll coordinate with Priya on access.
00:07:22 Priya Patel: noted, I can provision a staging VPC and a bastion for the test. We'll need the exact CIDR ranges.
00:07:27 Diego Ramos: I'll send the CIDR and port list in the checklist.
00:07:30 Liam O'Connor: any limitations with long-tail prompts or multi-tool calls? we do a lot of function-calling in product.
00:07:38 Diego Ramos: good question. Function/tool calling increases payload sizes and can blow up token count; latency scales linearly with tokens but there is some overhead for structure validation. For heavy function-calling we recommend chunked responses or stream mode; streaming adds little extra latency and helps perceived response time.
00:07:58 Maya Chen: also note our model variants support structured tool calling; we'll include a sample integration snippet.
00:08:05 Evan Brooks: security again — where are logs stored and retention?
00:08:09 Maya Chen: for hosted we retain logs per your retention policy and can push to your GCS/S3; for private/on-prem logs stay in your infra. We'll include audit log config in the security pack.
00:08:20 Priya Patel: great. can you confirm SSO/SAML and RBAC?
00:08:24 Maya Chen: yes SAML SSO supported, RBAC with org-level roles and per-route permissions. We'll share admin docs.
00:08:32 Liam O'Connor: ok can we get a targeted run focusing on the 40% 512-1024 sequence part? that's what stresses our system most.
00:08:39 Diego Ramos: yes we can run with a skewed mix. For that distribution our p99 at 1k rps went up to 520ms on q8, 460ms on q4, again with small quality tradeoffs on q4. We'll annotate the specific prompts that regressed.
00:09:00 Maya Chen: slight note on our naming of model variants — the export has small mismatches, Diego will reconcile naming and include mapping to your baseline model names in the sheet.
00:09:10 Diego Ramos: will do.
00:09:12 Evan Brooks: timeline — if we do on-prem week of 3/16 when can we expect results?
00:09:17 Diego Ramos: typically 3 business days of runs plus analysis so end of week 3/20ish, earlier if we parallelize.
00:09:23 Priya Patel: that works. we need the test harness earlier to vet it.
00:09:27 Diego Ramos: I'll upload the harness tomorrow.
00:09:30 Liam O'Connor: a couple of nitty gritty questions: did you simulate cold cache evictions, and how do you handle KV sharding?
00:09:36 Diego Ramos: yes we have a cold-start test that clears KV and measures first-request latency; sharding is horizontal across GPUs with consistent hashing for keys, which keeps per-GPU KV sizes bounded. We'll include a doc.
00:09:50 Maya Chen: any concerns on the customer side about model quality regression in quantized runs?
00:09:55 Liam O'Connor: yes we need to preserve clinical accuracy at least within 1-2% of baseline. So quantization will be limited to non-critical flows unless evals show parity.
00:10:08 Diego Ramos: understood. we'll report exact eval deltas per prompt.
00:10:12 Evan Brooks: can Redwood do a canary rollout so we can test subset of traffic in production?
00:10:16 Maya Chen: yes our rollout supports canary/A-B and automatic fallback to baseline if error rates exceed threshold. We'll configure threshold with you.
00:10:26 Priya Patel: nice. what's the turnaround for pricing for a dedicated reserved offer?
00:10:30 Maya Chen: I can draft a preliminary dedicated pricing deck by 3/9 once we have committed qps and model selection.
00:10:37 Liam O'Connor: perfect.
00:10:40 Diego Ramos: quick callout — in one of the runs BaselineCloud had a much higher variance that looked like network jitter. We recommend running tests in a controlled staging VPC to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
00:10:58 Priya Patel: agreed.
00:11:00 Maya Chen: let's recap next steps and owners. (recap) Maya send spreadsheet and security pack by 3/04; Diego send harness and on-prem checklist by 3/03; Liam to share dataset distribution by 3/06; Priya to provision staging access by 3/10; Schedule on-prem run week of 3/16.
00:11:21 Evan Brooks: sounds good. thanks.
00:11:23 Liam O'Connor: thanks all.
00:11:25 Maya Chen: thanks everyone we'll follow up in email with links to docs.
00:11:30 transcript note: auto captions sometimes mis-attribute or drop punctuation; full export attached in drive link.
